headline: Bruins place James Hagens on injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Bruins have placed James Hagens on injured reserve and called up Mike Eyssimont from Providence of the AHL. The report doesn't say what the injury is or how long he'll be out.

The timing stings for a young player who was producing. Hagens, the 7th overall pick in 2025, has 6 goals and 12 points in 17 games so far this season, but we'd temper that a little: his own expected goals (the quality of his chances) are 3.9, so he's scored 2.1 more than that. Still, Boston controls 54.7 percent of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is 2.7 points better with him than without. That's a real two-way contribution at 13.3 minutes a night. Boston sits at 12-4-1 and has leaned on goaltending (12.6 goals saved above expected) more than chance quality, with a 50.7 percent overall expected goal share, so losing a useful second-liner matters at the margins. Going by how the coach has used his players, Elias Lindholm (18:08 a night) is next in line for Hagens' minutes, and Eyssimont's call-up gives Boston a body but not a like-for-like replacement.
